title: Platform Data Architect Certification - Practice Exam
description: 60-question timed practice exam mirroring the official blueprint domain weights. 105 minutes, pass with 58% or higher.

questions.question: Partners must see only the accounts they own through a lookup on their Experience Cloud user record, at high volume. Which mechanism is most appropriate?
options: A criteria-based sharing rule per partner
Sharing sets bound to the lookup relationship
Manual sharing granted by an admin
Public read-only OWD on Account
questions.explanation: Sharing sets scale to high-volume portal access via a lookup; per-partner rules (A), manual sharing (C) and public OWD (D) do not scale or violate the constraint.

questions.question: A service org's Case object has 200M rows and slow list views; 95% of cases are closed and only referenced for compliance lookups. What is the best design?
options: Increase the Case object's index and keep all rows
Archive closed cases older than the retention threshold to a Big Object and delete them from Case
Move all cases to a Big Object immediately
Enable Salesforce Connect over Case
questions.explanation: Archiving old closed cases wins back LDV performance while retaining compliance data; raising limits (A) does not solve scale, moving all cases (C) breaks interactive use, and Connect (D) virtualizes rather than resolves volume.

questions.question: A team needs Opportunity line items to inherit the Opportunity's owner and sharing, and to roll up total line revenue onto the Opportunity. Which relationship type and feature combination should the architect recommend?
options: Lookup relationship plus a Flow to copy the owner and a scheduled Apex roll-up
Master-detail relationship plus a Roll-Up Summary field on Opportunity
Lookup relationship plus a Roll-Up Summary field on Opportunity
Master-detail relationship plus a formula field on Opportunity summarizing children
questions.explanation: Master-detail is required for native roll-ups and for automatic sharing/owner inheritance; a lookup cannot drive a native roll-up summary.

questions.question: Why is denormalization sometimes a skew mitigation rather than a cost?
options: It encrypts records to avoid locks
It removes the need for a hot parent lookup on frequent paths by carrying the value on the child
It moves records to a Big Object
It increases the fan-out to the parent
questions.explanation: Denormalizing the value onto children removes hot-path parent access and its locking; it does not encrypt (A), archive (C), or increase fan-out (D).

questions.question: Which TWO statements about a lookup relationship (vs master-detail) are TRUE?
options: The child inherits the parent's sharing rules
The child record can exist without a parent
Native roll-up summary fields are supported on the parent
Roll-up summaries must be replaced with Flow, Apex, or declarative rollup alternatives
questions.explanation: Lookups allow orphan children and do not inherit parent sharing (so A and C are false for lookups); the absence of native roll-ups is the reason D is true.

questions.question: An architect is told that deferring sharing calculation during a bulk load is required. Why?
options: It encrypts the data during load
It avoids re-running sharing recalculation for every batched insert, which is expensive under skew
It bypasses duplicate rules
It enables Big Object ingestion
questions.explanation: Deferring sharing defers the expensive recalculation until after the load; it does not encrypt (A), bypass duplicates (C), or relate to Big Objects (D).

questions.question: An auditor asks 'which systems and transformations produced this revenue value, and which reports consume it?' Which metadata artifact answers this?
options: The business glossary
Data lineage
The taxonomy
The object data dictionary
questions.explanation: Lineage traces origin-through-transformation-to-consumption; the glossary (A) defines terms, taxonomy (C) classifies, and the data dictionary (D) documents structure, not the flow.

questions.question: Which TWO factors contribute to data skew problems?
options: A single owner/queue holding a very large share of records
A large number of child records all referencing one parent record
A private organization-wide default
A shallow role hierarchy
questions.explanation: Ownership skew (A) and lookup skew (B) are the two named skew types; private OWD (C) and a shallow hierarchy (D) do not cause skew.

questions.question: Which TWO are examples of business metadata rather than technical metadata?
options: The field data type and maximum length
The business definition of 'Active Customer'
The data steward responsible for the domain
The API endpoint and object name
questions.explanation: Business definition (B) and steward ownership (C) are business metadata; data type/length (A) and API endpoint/object name (D) are technical metadata.

questions.question: An architect needs to know which users changed a validation rule last quarter. Which native tool answers this?
options: Field History Tracking
The Setup Audit Trail
The Metadata API
Data Loader
questions.explanation: The Setup Audit Trail records configuration changes by user/date; field history (A) tracks record data, the Metadata API (C) is for retrieval/deploy, and Data Loader (D) moves records.

questions.question: A company needs a child object visible to all users even when the parent account is restricted. Which design satisfies this?
options: Master-detail relationship to the parent
Lookup relationship plus owner-based sharing on the child
Change the parent OWD to public
Use a polymorphic lookup
questions.explanation: A lookup decouples child sharing from the parent and owner-based sharing opens the child (B); MD would force inheritance of the restricted parent (A), and opening the parent (C) violates the requirement.

questions.question: A model must be designed so a child record is visible to the same users as its parent, with no extra sharing rules. Which relationship choice achieves this natively?
options: Lookup relationship with owner-based sharing rules
Master-detail relationship
A polymorphic lookup
A junction object with two lookups
questions.explanation: Master-detail children inherit the parent's sharing and ownership; a lookup would require explicit sharing rules (A), and polymorphic/junction designs do not grant implicit inheritance (C, D).

questions.question: Which TWO statements about Person Accounts are TRUE?
options: They are ideal when modeling individual consumers alongside business accounts
Enablement can be toggled on and off per record type
They pair a single Account and Contact record for the same person
Enablement is org-wide and effectively irreversible
questions.explanation: Person Accounts suit B2C individual modeling (A) and are org-wide/irreversible (D); they are not toggled per record type (B false), and the pairing statement (C) is true as a fact but the question asks for the scenario-relevant pair - A and D capture the design trade-off.

questions.question: A sales org wants a private baseline but needs a manager to see all records owned by people below them in two different business units. What is the correct mechanism?
options: A public read/write OWD on the object
The role hierarchy, which grants upward visibility to managers
A manual 'share with peers' rule
Territory management, which is the only way to grant manager visibility
questions.explanation: The role hierarchy grants upward visibility to managers (B); public read/write violates the private baseline (A) and territory is an alternative for different scenarios, not the only way (D).

questions.question: Why is mass-reparenting high-volume children dangerous under skew?
options: It changes the record's data type
It fans out locking and cascade operations across millions of children, causing timeouts and lock errors
It disables validation rules
It removes external IDs
questions.explanation: Reparenting under skew spreads lock/cascade load across millions of records, causing timeouts; it does not change data types, disable validation, or remove external IDs.

questions.question: A golden record is established for Account, but the telephony system is authoritative for phone numbers. What does this imply?
options: Account is not really the golden record
System of truth is attribute-level: Account masters the record, telephony masters phone
Phone must be removed from Salesforce
A second Account golden record is needed
questions.explanation: Golden records are often composite with per-attribute authoritative sources; the record can still be mastered in Salesforce while one attribute is sourced elsewhere.

questions.question: A single org receives customer records from a portal (with a stable portal ID) and from manual entry (no ID). What is the best identity-resolution approach?
options: Fuzzy matching for all records
Deterministic matching on the portal external ID for portal records, fuzzy matching for manual records
Block all manual entry
Merge every record with a similar name
questions.explanation: Use deterministic external-ID matching where a stable key exists and fuzzy matching only where it does not; fuzzy-for-all (A) is weaker, and blocking entry or name-only merging is wrong (C, D).

questions.question: For the legal name attribute, the legal/ERP system must win even if the CRM value is newer. Which survivorship approach expresses this?
options: Most recent value always wins
A composed ordered rule: legal name from ERP, else most recent validated CRM name
Longest value wins
Whichever source has more fields populated
questions.explanation: Composed ordered survivorship rules encode 'ERP wins for legal name, with fallbacks'; pure recency (A) contradicts the requirement, and length/completeness are weaker fallbacks (C, D).

questions.question: Which TWO considerations are TRUE when choosing an integration user license?
options: API access is included on every license type and edition
A dedicated integration license/user should be secured with a Named Credential
API entitlement can vary by edition and license type
Integration users must have a full CRM license to write to custom objects
questions.explanation: Securing the integration user with a Named Credential (B) is best practice and API entitlement varies (C); API is not universally included (A false) and custom-object writes are allowed on Platform licenses (D false).

questions.question: Why is a single, hard match threshold risky when deduplicating customers who share household emails?
options: It has no relationship to matching
It can over-merge distinct people or under-merge, so a review band is safer
It disables duplicate rules
It prevents external IDs from working
questions.explanation: A hard threshold cannot distinguish household vs individual, so a review band lets a steward adjudicate ambiguous cases; the other options are unrelated or false.

questions.question: Which TWO techniques are essential to a single view of the customer across four systems?
options: A shared identity (external IDs/cross-reference) across systems
Each system independently authoring the same attributes
A defined system of record per attribute with one-way write propagation
Polling every system hourly
questions.explanation: Shared identity (A) and attribute-level system-of-record with one-way propagation (C) prevent conflicts; independent authoring (B) causes loops and polling (D) does not create a single view.

questions.question: Which TWO mechanisms preserve referential integrity on a lookup relationship?
options: Lookup filters restricting eligible parent records
A dependent picklist on the lookup field
Master-detail relationship with cascade behavior and/or required lookup
A page layout with the field marked read-only
questions.explanation: Lookup filters limit eligible parents (A) and master-detail/required lookups enforce the relationship's existence and delete behavior (C); dependent picklists constrain values, not relationships (B), and read-only layouts are UI-only (D).

questions.question: A nightly integration sometimes fails midway and is re-run. Which persistence pattern prevents duplicate records on re-run?
options: Insert with a duplicate rule alert
Upsert keyed on a stable external ID
Delete-then-insert each night
Load with the Data Loader 'insert' operation
questions.explanation: Upsert on a stable external ID is idempotent - re-running updates existing records instead of creating duplicates; insert (A, D) duplicates on retry and delete-then-insert (C) risks data loss and churn.

questions.question: Downstream systems must react to Salesforce Account changes within seconds without polling. Which native mechanism is best?
options: Scheduled nightly export
Change Data Capture change events via the streaming API
Field Audit Trail
Data Loader export
questions.explanation: CDC publishes change events in near real time; nightly export (A) and Data Loader (D) are batch, and Field Audit Trail (C) is compliance history, not propagation.

questions.question: An integration loads Accounts then their Contacts across four source systems. What ordering/key design is best?
options: Load Contacts first, then Accounts
Upsert Accounts first (keyed on composite external ID), then Contacts resolving the parent by external ID
Insert all records in one parallel job without keys
Load only Accounts and skip Contacts
questions.explanation: Parent-first upsert with composite keys and parent resolution by external ID satisfies referential integrity and idempotency; other options break ordering or identity.

questions.question: During an org consolidation, downstream systems break because record IDs changed. What should have prevented this?
options: Enabling more duplicate rules
Using external IDs/cross-references to relink records and keep downstream links valid
Turning off CDC
Increasing API limits
questions.explanation: Because Salesforce IDs are org-specific, a consolidation requires external IDs/cross-references to relink and re-key downstream systems; the other options do not preserve identity across orgs.

questions.question: A group needs only custom objects but also needs standard Activities and reporting on Accounts. What is the likely conclusion?
options: A Platform license suffices because reports are separate
The group likely needs a CRM license because it requires standard-object access
Custom objects can fully replace Accounts
Activities are available on all license types
questions.explanation: If the group must reach standard objects/features (Accounts/Activities reporting), a CRM license is required; custom objects cannot replace standard objects with platform features (C) and license ceilings still apply (A, D).

questions.question: Which TWO statements about keys in Salesforce integration are TRUE?
options: The Salesforce record Id is stable across orgs
A mutable natural key risks duplicating records when it changes
An external ID enables upsert and cross-system identity
Surrogate keys are meaningful to external systems
questions.explanation: Mutable natural keys can duplicate on change (B) and external IDs enable upsert/identity (C); the Salesforce Id differs across orgs (A false) and a surrogate Id is not meaningful externally (D false).

questions.question: The only requirement for three orgs is a unified customer dashboard; processes differ and stay separate. What is the best design?
options: Consolidate all three orgs
Unify reporting via Data Connect/warehouse while keeping orgs separate
Merge only the Accounts
Enable CDC on all orgs and delete two
questions.explanation: When the only need is reporting, unifying analytics (Data Connect/warehouse) satisfies it without the cost/risk of consolidation; consolidation (A) is overkill and the others do not meet the goal.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about merging in Salesforce are TRUE?
options: Related records are reparented to the surviving record
The merge is fully reversible at any time
Merging deletes the losing duplicate records
Mass merge at high volume is a native batch feature
questions.explanation: Merging reparents children (A) and deletes losers (C); it is not freely reversible (B) and native mass-merge at scale is not a standard batch feature (D).

questions.question: A warehouse operations team needs to create and edit a custom 'Shipment__c' object but has no need for Accounts or Opportunities. Which license is most cost-effective?
options: Sales Cloud
Service Cloud
Salesforce Platform
Partner Community
questions.explanation: Platform licenses grant custom-object access without the cost of core CRM objects; Sales/Service (A, B) are unnecessary and Partner Community (D) is for external partners.

questions.question: An integration user must call REST APIs to load data into custom objects only. Which license minimizes cost while meeting the need?
options: A full Sales Cloud license
A Platform/Integration license
A Partner Community license
A Customer Community license
questions.explanation: Platform/Integration licenses serve API-only users on custom objects; full CRM (A) is wasteful and community licenses (C, D) are for external persons with restricted access.

questions.question: Why is Field Audit Trail needed in addition to CDC when building a single customer view?
options: Because CDC cannot handle more than one object
Because CDC propagates changes while Field Audit Trail provides long-term compliance change history
Because Field Audit Trail replaces external IDs
Because CDC only works for Contacts
questions.explanation: CDC is for system propagation; compliance retention of who-changed-what needs Audit Trail (and Field Audit Trail/history) - they are complementary.

questions.question: Which operating model keeps enterprise standards central while domains execute day-to-day governance?
options: Fully centralized
Fully federated
Hybrid (central standards, domain execution)
No formal model
questions.explanation: Hybrid combines central standards with domain execution and is the common enterprise choice; centralized (A) bottlenecks and federated (B) risks inconsistency.

questions.question: Which TWO platform capabilities directly protect personal data at rest and in access control?
options: Shield Platform Encryption for sensitive fields
Field-level security and permission sets to restrict access
A page layout marked read-only
A duplicate rule
questions.explanation: Shield Platform Encryption (A) and FLS/permission sets (B) are direct protection controls; read-only layouts and duplicate rules are not protection controls.

questions.question: Which TWO dimensions describe data quality that a governance scorecard should track?
options: Completeness and uniqueness
CPU utilization and disk throughput
Consistency and timeliness
Number of page layouts
questions.explanation: Completeness/uniqueness (A) and consistency/timeliness (C) are core data-quality dimensions; infrastructure and layout counts are not data-quality measures.

questions.question: A governance program measures a 22% duplicate rate on Accounts but duplicates persist. What is the missing component?
options: More metrics
An issue-management workflow with owners and SLAs to resolve the duplicates
A larger data dictionary
Platform Encryption
questions.explanation: Metrics identify the problem; resolution needs a workflow with accountability and SLAs. More metrics (A) or a bigger dictionary (C) do not fix data, and encryption (D) is unrelated.

questions.question: A customer processes data under consent for marketing. A subject withdraws consent. What must the data model support?
options: Nothing; consent is informal
Recording consent state and stopping processing (marketing) on withdrawal
Deleting the entire customer record immediately
Encrypting the marketing field
questions.explanation: Consent withdrawal must halt the consented processing (marketing); it does not necessarily require deleting the whole record (C), and encoding/encryption (D) do not honor withdrawal.

questions.question: Which TWO are true considerations when enabling Platform Encryption on a field?
options: Some filters, sorts, and roll-ups may behave differently on encrypted fields
Encryption has no effect on any platform function
Deterministic encryption supports certain exact-match operations within limits
Encryption removes the need for field-level security
questions.explanation: Encryption changes some function behavior (A) and deterministic schemes allow limited exact-match operations (C); it does not leave functions untouched (B) nor replace FLS (D).

questions.question: Which TWO are constraints of External Objects?
options: They require an External ID as the external key
They support roll-up summary fields
They cannot be the child in a master-detail with standard objects
They are always faster than native objects
questions.explanation: External Objects need an External ID (A) and cannot be the child of a master-detail with standard objects (C); they do not support roll-ups (B) and are not inherently faster (D).

questions.question: Why is age + status the most common archival selection criterion?
options: It is the only supported pattern
It is auditable, maps to retention policy, and targets genuinely cold records
It avoids the need to delete records
It requires no testing
questions.explanation: Age + status is auditable and aligns to retention, targeting cold records; it is not the only pattern (A), still requires deletion (C), and must be tested (D).

questions.question: Why must LDV performance be validated in a full sandbox at representative volume?
options: Because sandbox data is encrypted
Because LDV issues only manifest at scale and small datasets hide them
Because production cannot be tested
Because record types differ in production
questions.explanation: LDV behavior is volume-dependent, so realistic volume is required; encryption (A), production access (C), and record types (D) are not the reason.

questions.question: A customer must purge customer data to satisfy GDPR storage limitation but also retain financial transactions for 7 years. What is the best plan?
options: Delete all data older than one year
Anonymize personal fields on transactions older than the retention point while retaining the financial records for 7 years
Archive everything to a Big Object with no deletion
Retain everything indefinitely
questions.explanation: Anonymize-and-retain satisfies erasure of personal data while preserving required financial records; indiscriminate deletion (A) breaks retention rules, and B/D violate storage limitation.

questions.question: A parent org is authoritative for Accounts and changes constantly; a subsidiary org needs to view them live in Salesforce. What is the best approach?
options: Nightly copy into the subsidiary
Expose the parent org's Accounts as External Objects via the cross-org adapter
Merge the two orgs
Export to CSV weekly
questions.explanation: The cross-org adapter gives live cross-org access without copying; nightly/weekly copies (A, D) are stale and merging (C) is a bigger change than the requirement.

questions.question: A list view filters Cases by 'Status != Closed' on a 10-million-row object and is slow. What is the best redesign?
options: Add more columns to the list view
Redesign to filter on an indexed positive field (e.g., an indexed status/open flag) and archive old closed cases
Sort the list view by a formula field
Convert Case to a Big Object
questions.explanation: Negative filters can be non-selective; a positive indexed filter plus archiving bounds the set. Adding columns/sorting by formula (A, C) do not fix selectivity, and Big Objects (D) would break interactive use.

questions.question: Why choose an off-platform archive store over an on-platform Big Object for some data categories?
options: It keeps data editable in Salesforce
It frees Salesforce storage when the platform does not need to serve the data
It supports standard reports natively
It avoids the need for retention rules
questions.explanation: Off-platform archiving frees Salesforce storage when native query is not required; it is not directly editable (A), does not add native reports (C), and never removes retention obligations (D).

questions.question: Which TWO should be part of an archiving/purging plan for a parent object with millions of child records?
options: Handle referential integrity by archiving children or rerouting lookups
Delete the parent and leave dangling child lookups
Define retention per data category with any legal hold
Disable audit logging to speed the job
questions.explanation: Referential-integrity handling (A) and per-category retention with legal hold (C) are essential; dangling lookups (B) corrupt data and disabling audit logging (D) removes the evidence.

questions.question: A report on a 5-million-row object times out because it filters on an unindexed custom text field. What is the most direct fix?
options: Add more fields to the report
Request a custom index on the filter field (or add a skinny table for the reported fields)
Reduce the report's columns
Enable Big Objects for the object
questions.explanation: A custom index (or skinny table) makes the filter selective; reducing columns (C) does not fix selectivity, and Big Objects (D) would require moving the data.

questions.question: A company needs live visibility of volatile ERP order history but Salesforce must run fast reports only on active orders. What is the best design?
options: Copy all order history into Salesforce
Copy the stable active orders and virtualize the full history via an External Object
Virtualize everything including active orders
Disable reporting on orders
questions.explanation: A hybrid copies the small stable/hot subset for native reporting and virtualizes the large volatile history; copying all (A) wastes storage and virtualizing the hot active orders (C) loses native speed.

questions.question: Which TWO fields are natively indexed by the platform?
options: A standard text field holding free-form notes
OwnerId
CreatedDate / SystemModstamp
A multi-select picklist
questions.explanation: OwnerId (B) and CreatedDate/SystemModstamp (C) are natively indexed; free-text (A) and multi-select picklists (D) are not indexed efficiently.

questions.question: Which TWO scenarios argue for COPYING rather than virtualizing?
options: Users must run approvals, validation, and fast reports on the data
The data must remain only in the source for residency
The source system is slow and the data is stable
The data changes every second and is only ever read
questions.explanation: Native automation/speed needs (A) and a slow source with stable data (C) favor copying; residency (B) and high-volatility read-only data (D) favor virtualization.

questions.question: A cutover's final delta sync is taking far longer than planned because change volume since the last sync was underestimated. What was missing?
options: A larger batch size
A rehearsed, timed cutover runbook that measured the final delta sync realistically
More duplicate rules
A Big Object archive
questions.explanation: Only a rehearsed, timed runbook reveals realistic delta duration; batch size, duplicate rules, and archives do not address cutover timing.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about Salesforce exports are TRUE?
options: Report exports are limited by row limits and not suited to LDV
Exports include all data regardless of the running user's access
Scheduled Data Export is a coarse backup, not a full point-in-time restore
Exports can be non-selective without performance impact
questions.explanation: Report exports have row limits (A) and Data Export is coarse backup only (C); exports are filtered by the user's access (B false) and LDV exports must be selective (D false).

questions.question: Which TWO elements make up a reliable migration quality gate?
options: A versioned source-to-target mapping document
A page layout matching the source fields
Reconciliation of source vs loaded counts plus a rejects/error file
Disabling target validation rules during load
questions.explanation: A versioned mapping (A) and count reconciliation with an error file (C) are the quality gates; layouts are irrelevant and disabling validation defeats quality.

questions.question: Which activity belongs to post-go-live validation rather than pre-cutover?
options: Profiling the source data
Dry-run load in a full sandbox
Reconciling counts/aggregates and validating integrations and access after go-live
Writing the mapping document
questions.explanation: Post-go-live validation reconciles counts, validates integrations, and checks access on the live system; profiling/ dry-run / mapping are pre-migration activities.

questions.question: Why is incremental migration often chosen for large, business-critical programs?
options: It eliminates the need for a delta sync
It reduces risk and downtime by moving data in waves while testing between them
It avoids all data-quality work
It requires no rollback plan
questions.explanation: Waves reduce risk and allow learning, though they require parallel-run sync (A false); quality work (C) and rollback planning (D) are still required.

questions.question: Why must large exports filter on indexed fields?
options: Because exports cannot use SOQL
Because non-selective queries time out at LDV, so indexed filters keep extraction performant
Because reports require it
Because encryption requires it
questions.explanation: LDV exports must be selective to avoid timeouts; exports do use SOQL (A false) and the other reasons are unrelated.

questions.question: Which TWO are required before deleting data from Salesforce after an archival export?
options: Verify the export is complete and restorable/queryable
Delete immediately to free storage
Reconcile exported counts against Salesforce
Encrypt the source records in place
questions.explanation: Completeness/restorability verification (A) and count reconciliation (C) must precede deletion; deleting first (B) risks data loss and in-place encryption (D) is unrelated.

questions.question: A 12-million-row load fails with 'unable to obtain row lock' when Contacts and their parent Accounts load concurrently. Which change most directly fixes this?
options: Increase the batch size
Load parents first and use serial mode (or group by parent) to avoid lock contention
Switch to the synchronous SOAP API
Disable duplicate rules
questions.explanation: Parent lock contention is solved by ordering/grouping by parent and using serial mode; bigger batches (A) worsen it, synchronous APIs (C) are slower, and duplicate rules (D) are unrelated.

questions.question: A warehouse feed pulls changed records by SystemModstamp but never reflects deletions. What is the fix?
options: Increase the batch size
Use Change Data Capture delete events or run a periodic id-set reconciliation to detect deletes
Switch to report exports
Enable duplicate rules
questions.explanation: Last-modified extracts miss deletes; CDC delete events or reconciliation detects them. Batch size, report exports, and duplicate rules do not address deletions.
